precepts.text: Solomon determines to build a house for the name of the Lord and numbers the bearers, hewers, and overseers, sending to Hiram to deal with him as he dealt with David, because the house is for burning incense, showbread, and the offerings on the sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, an ordinance forever for Israel.
precepts.point: This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon was able to say deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built. It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.” He told out “threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

Then he sent to Huram the king of Tyre: “As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.” This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon could say, deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built.

The house was for the name of the Lord, “to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

So Hiram gave cedar and fir, Solomon gave wheat and pure oil year by year, and “there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.” It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

precepts.text: Hiram answers in writing, blessing the Lord God of Israel, and sends a cunning man named Huram whose father was a man of Tyre and whose mother was of the daughters of Dan, skillful to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, and fine linen, showing that Hiram and his craftsman were joined to Israel by lineage.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the Lord hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them.” He said, “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.”

Hiram sent “a cunning man, endued with understanding”, “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson”.

Hiram and his craftsman were joined to Israel by lineage: the craftsman’s mother was of the daughters of Dan. That is part of why there was peace between Hiram and Solomon and they two made a league together, and why “the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him” is seen in how he dealt with Hiram.

precepts.text: Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, with three thousand six hundred to oversee them, the same ordered labor described here.
precepts.point: Solomon had order in the work, with bearers of burdens, hewers in the mountains, and above them the chief of his officers, thirty-three hundred who ruled over the people that wrought. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure without murmuring over who did which task.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom. And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

That is the same ordered labor described here: “threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains”, and over them the chief of Solomon’s officers, “which ruled over the people that wrought in the work.” Solomon had order in the work, bearers, hewers and overseers.

The levy was an enlistment for service, thirty thousand men sent to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses, “a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home”, gathered to bring the wood back to Jerusalem, with Adoniram over the levy. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure, without murmuring over who did which task.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, for the Lord searcheth all hearts.
precepts.point: David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the Lord searcheth all hearts.” And David warned him: “if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.”

“Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord.” Where did Solomon get this understanding and this vision? It came from his father David, who charged him to build the house.

precepts.text: David gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.
precepts.point: David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat.”

Solomon did not come up with the house on his own. David charged him to build it and gave him the pattern. So when “Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord”, and told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them, he was carrying out what his father had given him.

precepts.text: Two lambs of the first year without spot were offered day by day for a continual burnt offering.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“This is the offering made by fire which ye shall offer unto the Lord; two lambs of the first year without spot day by day, for a continual burnt offering.”

The daily offering was two lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening. That is what Solomon named: “the burnt offerings morning and evening.” “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

precepts.text: On the sabbath day two lambs of the first year were offered, beside the continual burnt offering.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof.”

The sabbath offering added two more lambs beside the continual burnt offering. Solomon built the house for the burnt offerings “on the sabbaths” as well, and “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot.”

The beginning of the months is the new moon, and it had its own burnt offering. Solomon named it with the rest: “on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.” That is why we keep them in the land of our captivity, according to the law given through Moses in the book of Numbers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And in the fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord.”

After the daily, sabbath and new moon offerings come the solemn feasts, beginning with the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, and the feast of unleavened bread beginning the fifteenth day. These are “the solemn feasts of the Lord our God” Solomon built the house for, and “This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.”

At even: the day is reckoned from even to even. So the passover is kept at even on the fourteenth, and the feast of unleavened bread begins the fifteenth day. These are among the solemn feasts Solomon named, ordained forever to Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel.”

The offerings Solomon named, “morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God”, are “an ordinance for ever to Israel.” That is why we keep them in the land of our captivity: in the places of drawing water we rehearse the righteous acts of the Most High, according to the law given through Moses.

precepts.text: The workman was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, his father a man of Tyre, filled with wisdom to work in brass.
precepts.point: Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“He was a widow’s son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass.”

Chronicles says the same workman was “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre.” There is no contradiction. His mother was of the tribe of Naphtali, but she was of the city of Dan, which lay within the land of Naphtali. This is cleared up by using the Bible dictionary and the maps, and by chasing the references.

He was “skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving.”

precepts.text: The children of Dan called the name of the city Dan after their father, though the name of the city was Laish at the first.
precepts.point: Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.”

That is the city of Dan the workman's mother came from. The children of Dan took Laish and renamed it after their father. Israel had put the nations to tribute rather than driving them out as the Lord commanded, but the city itself sat in the borders of Naphtali, so a woman there could be spoken of both ways: a widow “of the tribe of Naphtali”, and “a woman of the daughters of Dan.”

precepts.text: The children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, and called it Dan after the name of their father.
precepts.point: Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.”

Leshem is Laish, the same city. Joshua and Judges together show how a city named Dan came to stand within the borders of Naphtali, and why Huram's mother is called “of the daughters of Dan” in Chronicles and “of the tribe of Naphtali” in Kings.

precepts.text: The Lord promised David a son, Solomon, who would be a man of rest, having peace and quietness given to Israel in his days.
precepts.point: David had prepared for the house long before, telling Solomon that in his trouble he had laid up a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, brass and iron without weight, timber and stone, and workmen in abundance. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.”

The Lord promised David a son who would be a man of rest, with peace and quietness given to Israel in his days. In that rest Solomon built, setting the strangers in the land to work, “threescore and ten thousand of them to be bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work.”

precepts.text: In his trouble David prepared for the house of the Lord gold, silver, brass, iron, timber, and stone in abundance.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Now, behold, in my trouble I have prepared for the house of the Lord an hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver; and of brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance: timber also and stone have I prepared; and thou mayest add thereto.”

David had prepared for the house long before. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials. Even the numbering of the strangers was “after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them.”

precepts.text: Israel is told to go forth out of the city, for this is not our rest while our enemies still afflict us.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.”

Solomon was a man of rest, and in his days Israel had peace and quietness, and the strangers in the land were set to Israel's work. Israel is told to go forth out of the city, for this is not our rest while our enemies still afflict us. There the Lord shall redeem us from the hand of our enemies.
